items.title: Three Steps to the Terminal: A Siemens ROX II Zero-Day Trilogy
items.feed_description: A technical analysis of three chained zero-day vulnerabilities in Siemens ROX II OT switches that allow privilege escalation and persistent root access. The post Three Steps to the Terminal: A Siemens ROX II Zero-Day Trilogy appeared first on Unit 42 .
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers, in collaboration with Siemens, discovered three zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-40947, CVE-2025-40948, CVE-2025-40949) in Siemens ROX II OT switches. These vulnerabilities enable privilege escalation, command injection, and persistent root access via a chained exploit. Siemens released firmware updates (V2.17.1) to address the issues, and Palo Alto Networks provides virtual patching detection for affected devices.
features: Three zero-day vulnerabilities in Siemens ROX II OT switches (CVE-2025-40947, CVE-2025-40948, CVE-2025-40949)

Firmware update recommendation: Siemens SSA-973901, SSA-078743, SSA-081142 (V2.17.1)
Palo Alto Networks virtual patching detection via Next-Generation Firewall with Advanced Threat Prevention
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must prioritize updating Siemens ROX II switches to firmware V2.17.1 to mitigate critical privilege escalation risks. Organizations should leverage virtual patching and monitoring tools to detect and prevent exploitation of similar vulnerabilities in OT environments.

items.title: AI Security Is Never Finished: Building the Continuous Red Teaming Loop
items.feed_description: Security programs are built around moments of closure: the finding is closed, the control passed, and the release can move forward. AI security refuses to cooperate with that model. A passing test is useful evidence, but only for a specific system, configuration, and moment. Production AI keeps moving. Models change behavior, prompts are revised, retrieval sources are added, agents gain tools, and users introduce unexpected context. Attackers adapt just as quickly. Yesterday’s clean result may not describe tomorrow’s risk. That has been the practical case for continuous AI red teaming. Now, research from the National Institute of Standards and Technology […] The post AI Security Is Never Finished: Building the Continuous Red Teaming Loop appeared first on Check Point Blog .
items.summary: Check Point highlights the limitations of traditional AI security models, emphasizing the need for continuous red teaming due to AI's evolving nature. Based on NIST research, the company outlines a framework requiring ongoing adversarial testing, system hardening, and operational resilience to address dynamic threats. The approach shifts from static guardrails to a feedback loop of discovery, improvement, and real-time protection.
features: Continuous adversarial discovery for identifying attack paths
Continuous hardening to address discovered vulnerabilities
Operational resilience to limit exploit impact
Feedback loop integrating testing, protection, and monitoring
Integration with Check Point AI Defense Plane for runtime protection
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must adopt continuous testing and adaptation to counter AI's evolving threats, moving beyond static defenses to proactive, real-time protection and improvement cycles.

items.title: TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development
items.feed_description: TuxBot v3 Evolution, an IoT botnet framework built with LLMs. Read our analysis of its cross-compiled binaries, C2 architecture and bugs. The post TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development appeared first on Unit 42 .
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers uncovered TuxBot v3, a modular IoT botnet framework leveraging LLM-assisted development with functional C2 infrastructure, DGA, P2P communication, and cross-architecture exploitation capabilities. The framework includes a Go-based C2 server with DDoS-for-hire features, Docker test environments, and a XOR-encrypted string table with decryption bugs. Researchers identified 70% functional components, including Telnet brute-force, exploit code for 30+ IoT families, and a Git log indicating Iranian ties.
features: Modular IoT botnet framework with cross-architecture C2 capabilities
Go-based C2 server with DDoS-for-hire panel and SSH admin interface
SHA512 DGA and Ed25519-signed P2P gossip fallback mechanisms
Docker-based test infrastructure and QEMU multi-architecture testing
Telnet brute-force with 1,496 credential pairs
XOR-encrypted string table with key decryption bugs
Git log timeline showing development progression
Source code and compiled binaries for 17 architectures
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must enhance IoT device protection against LLM-assisted botnets using advanced URL filtering and DNS security. The XOR decryption bug and functional C2 infrastructure highlight the need for real-time threat intelligence and behavioral detection to mitigate potential DDoS and ransomware attacks from compromised IoT devices.

items.title: AI Agents are Only As Effective as Their Harness
items.feed_description: Every AI vendor is talking about agents – autonomous systems that handle complex tasks without constant human input. The promise is real. But one question gets asked too rarely: what makes an agent reliable enough to trust with your network security? The answer isn’t the model. It’s the harness. Agents Run on LLMs. Reliability Runs on Something Else AI agents get their reasoning power from large language models (LLMs). LLMs are impressive. They understand context, reason through complex problems, and plan across a wide range of tasks. But on its own, an LLM is a generalist. It knows a little about everything and not enough about your […] The post AI Agents are Only As Effective as Their Harness appeared first on Check Point Blog .
items.summary: Check Point emphasizes that AI agents' reliability in network security depends on their 'harness'—a framework combining skills, tools, and context. The company highlights its agentic platform built on LLMs but differentiated by a harness leveraging 30 years of real-world deployment expertise, a live network knowledge graph, and contextual awareness. This approach addresses hallucination risks by grounding AI decisions in up-to-date environment data and organizational policies.
features: Three-core harness components: skills, tools, and context
Proprietary Network Knowledge Graph for real-time environment mapping
Skills derived from 30+ years of enterprise security deployments
Contextual awareness integrating policies, dependencies, and regulatory requirements
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams benefit from reduced hallucination risks and more reliable AI-driven decisions through Check Point's harness approach, which ensures AI agents operate with accurate, context-aware insights from live network data rather than static training sets.

items.title: Email Agent Hijacking: The Hidden Threat That Breaks Post-Delivery Security
items.feed_description: Key takeaways AI agents create a new email attack surface because they can process content before humans see it Email Agent Hijacking hides instructions in email content to manipulate AI interpretation, decisions, or outputs Post-delivery controls are too late when an AI agent acts immediately after delivery Organizations need preventive protection for AI-consumed content and validation for AI-generated responses AI agents are now reading and writing emails before humans ever see them. What was once a human-centric communication channel is quickly becoming an AI-driven workflow, and that shift introduces a new and largely unprotected attack surface. Much of the industry’s recent attention has centered […] The post Email Agent Hijacking: The Hidden Threat That Breaks Post-Delivery Security appeared first on Check Point Blog .
items.summary: Check Point identifies 'Email Agent Hijacking' as a new threat exploiting AI agents that process emails before humans, creating an untapped attack surface. Attackers hide malicious instructions in email content to manipulate AI interpretations or outputs, bypassing traditional post-delivery security controls. The shift to AI-driven email workflows introduces risks where AI agents act immediately after delivery, rendering reactive measures ineffective. Organizations require preventive protections for AI-consumed content and validation of AI-generated responses to mitigate this threat.
features: Email Agent Hijacking: Exploits AI agents processing emails pre-human interaction
Hidden malicious instructions in email content to manipulate AI outputs
Post-delivery security controls are ineffective against immediate AI actions
Recommended preventive protections for AI-consumed content and response validation
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must prioritize defending against AI-driven email threats by implementing proactive content safeguards and validating AI-generated responses to prevent exploitation of new attack surfaces.

items.title: The Identity Problem Hiding in AI Agent Deployments
items.summary: CrowdStrike highlights the identity verification challenges in AI agent deployments, emphasizing the risk of unauthorized access and data exposure due to opaque authentication mechanisms. The blog underscores the need for robust identity management to secure AI-driven workflows.
features: Continuous Identity for AI Agents: Real-time identity validation for AI interactions.
Integration with OpenID and IDPro: Enhanced authentication protocols for agent-based systems.
Shadow AI Visibility Service: Monitoring and control over AI agent activities.
New detection capabilities for prompt injection attacks and unauthorized access attempts.
items.why_it_matters: SOC teams must address identity gaps in AI agents to prevent exploitation of weak authentication, ensuring secure and compliant AI deployments.

items.title: 94% of Organizations Report Cloud Breaches: CrowdStrike State of CDR Survey
items.summary: CrowdStrike's State of CDR survey reveals 94% of organizations experienced cloud breaches, citing poor cloud visibility, inability to distinguish legitimate/malicious activity, and fragmented detection/response as key challenges. The report underscores the urgent need for advanced cloud security solutions.
features: Falcon AIDR detects threats in Kubernetes AI apps
Falcon Cloud Security updates for Azure and Google Cloud
Shadow AI Visibility Service for cloud workload monitoring
Continuous Identity for AI agent access control
items.why_it_matters: Security teams face escalating risks from cloud misconfigurations and AI-driven attacks. CrowdStrike's updates address critical gaps in cloud visibility, threat detection, and identity management for modern infrastructure.
